message.content: {"facts": ["Empirical Mode (EM) hard for simple empirical models to meet the accuracy requirements of water quality parameters concentration estimation", "Poor generalities due to regional and temporal constraints", "Requires a lot of field water quality sampling data as the basis to assure relatively higher accuracy", "Analytical Mode (AM) composition of water body and radiation transmission procedure is rather complex", "Spectral resolution of most satellite sensors and those measured near the ground are inconsistent", "Quantitative remote sensing inversion based on the analytical mode is difficult to achieve and is limited in practical applications", "Semi-Empirical Mode (SEM) none mentioned in the paragraph", "Artificial Intelligence (AI) Mode establishing a neural network for water quality retrieval requires a large number of samples to be trained with extensive experiences", "Increase in the number of training samples will make SVM algorithms difficult to implement and run slowly", "Can Sentinel-2 satellite data combined with multiple machine learning algorithms be used to accurately retrieve inland water quality parameters?", "Machine learning algorithms, specifically random forest and support vector regression, combined with Sentinel-2 data can provide accurate retrieval of inland water quality parameters such as chlorophyll-a, total suspended solids, and turbidity", "Can the entire lifespan of MERIS satellite data combined with machine learning approaches be used to monitor the water quality of Valle de Bravo Reservoir in Mexico?", "Machine learning algorithms, specifically artificial neural networks and random forests, combined with the entire lifespan of MERIS data can accurately monitor the water quality of the Valle de Bravo Reservoir, including parameters such as chlorophyll-a, total suspended solids, and colored dissolved organic matter"]}
